headline: Faraday Shows Magnetism Itself Can Generate Electric Current
dispatch: London, August 29, 1831. Michael Faraday of the Royal Institution yesterday produced an electric current from a moving magnetic field, demonstrating that electricity could be induced without a battery or chemical cell. Working with a coiled iron ring and a sensitive galvanometer, Faraday recorded the deflection of the needle each time the magnetic circuit was broken or completed. The discovery establishes a new principle that may one day drive machines by magnetism alone.
